summary: Holcomb Hill tower in Chester, Mass.: current 60-foot steel tower; register dates it to 1934 CCC work but its own timeline implies 1944; fenced and unstaffed in 2016.

facts.design: Current 60-foot steel tower with a 10 by 10 foot aluminum cab, installed 1965

access.note: A large locked fence surrounds the tower per the May 2016 visit report. The register says it is off an unmarked road and outside any state park. No source says the public may climb it.

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

corrections.why: The register describes the current tower as a 60-foot steel structure. The wooden tower was the 1918 structure, not the one standing now.

notes_for_editor: Build year unresolved: the register says the CCC built the current tower in 1934, but says it replaced the 1918 tower 26 years later (1944). No second source found for the tower. Wikipedia's CCC 1934-1940 is about the forest, not the tower. The register says not in any state park; Chester-Blandford State Forest is a state forest, and the register does not say whether Holcomb Hill is inside it. Two fire-lookout history pages (firelookout.org, ffla.org) that search pointed to returned 404 from the crawl cache, so their details (Camp 64, Aermotor, ECW funds, 1918 tower from Sharon) are unverified and not used. Brief record had material wood; corrected to steel above. Height 60 ft converted to 18.3 m.
